definitions.explanation: The third month of the year. In Japan, this is graduation season and the end of the fiscal/school year.

examples.japanese: {三月|さんがつ}は{春|はる}です。
{三月|さんがつ}は{暖|あたた}かくなります。
{三月|さんがつ}から{桜|さくら}が{咲|さ}きます。
examples.english: Cherry blossoms start blooming from March.

examples.japanese: {三月|さんがつ}の{終|お}わりに{友|とも}だちと{花見|はなみ}をしました。
examples.english: I went flower viewing with friends at the end of March.

examples.japanese: {三月|さんがつ}になると、{公園|こうえん}に{桜|さくら}の{花|はな}がたくさん{咲|さ}いて、とてもきれいです。
examples.english: When March comes, many cherry blossoms bloom in the park, and it's very beautiful.

notes:
{三月|さんがつ} is the third month of the year.

JAPANESE MONTHS:
All months use number + {月|がつ}:
- {一月|いちがつ} (January) through {十二月|じゅうにがつ} (December)

MARCH SIGNIFICANCE:
- End of {学年|がくねん} (school year)
- End of {年度|ねんど} (fiscal year)
- {卒業|そつぎょう}シーズン: graduation season
- {送別会|そうべつかい}: farewell parties

MARCH EVENTS:
- {ひな祭|まつ}り (March 3): Girls' Day/Doll Festival
- {春分|しゅんぶん}の{日|ひ} (around March 21): Vernal Equinox Day
- {桜|さくら}の{開花|かいか}: cherry blossom blooming begins

SEASON:
March marks the transition from winter to spring ({春|はる}). {花見|はなみ} (cherry blossom viewing) begins in late March in many parts of Japan.
